question: In June 2025, the World Bank approved a ₹3,700 crore loan for lake rejuvenation in which of the following cities of India to aid flood resilience?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **World Bank** officially approved a massive loan amounting to **₹3,700 crore** (approximately **$440 million**) dedicated to the **rejuvenation of lakes** and the enhancement of **flood resilience** in **Bengaluru**.
 
• The project is specifically designed to address the recurring problem of **urban flooding** in the city, which is often caused by the mismanagement of **stormwater drains** and the degradation of natural water bodies. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bengaluru.***
 
• This initiative focuses on restoring the **interconnectivity** of the lake systems, which historically acted as a natural flood mitigation mechanism for the **Karnataka** state capital.
 
• The funding aims to support **nature-based solutions**, such as the creation of wetlands and the desilting of major **primary and secondary drains** (Rajakaluves) to ensure smooth water flow during heavy rainfall.
 
• The project is a collaborative effort between the **Government of Karnataka** and international financial institutions to transform the "Silicon Valley of India" into a climate-resilient megacity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The World Bank's Role in India**:
 
 
• The **World Bank** has been a long-term partner in India's urban development, providing technical expertise and **financial assistance** for infrastructure, **clean energy**, and **water management**.
 
• Headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, the organization focuses on sustainable development goals and poverty reduction through large-scale developmental loans.
 
 
 
• **Bengaluru's Lake Ecosystem**:
 
 
• **Bengaluru**, originally known as the "City of Lakes," once possessed over **200 lakes** that were interconnected to manage the undulating terrain's water runoff.
 
• Rapid **urbanization** and **encroachment** over the last few decades have led to the disappearance of many water bodies, contributing significantly to modern-day flooding.
 
 
 
• **Flood Resilience Strategies**:
 
 
• **Flood resilience** involves building infrastructure that can withstand extreme weather events. In **India**, cities like **Chennai** and **Mumbai** have also sought similar international funding to upgrade their **drainage systems**.
 
• Strategies often include **Integrated Urban Water Management (IUWM)**, which treats the entire urban water cycle as a single system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Execution**: The **Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)** and the **Karnataka Interior Department** are the primary agencies responsible for executing the rejuvenation works on the ground.
 
• **Impact on Groundwater**: Beyond flood control, the rejuvenation of these lakes is critical for **groundwater recharge**, as **Bengaluru** faces a severe **water crisis** during the summer months.
 
• **Environmental Benefits**: The restoration of lakes helps in maintaining **local biodiversity**, reducing the **urban heat island effect**, and providing recreational spaces for citizens.
 
• **Loan Terms**: The **₹3,700 crore** loan typically comes with a grace period and is part of the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)** lending portfolio for **India**.
